description: Drug CDSS (Clinical Decision Support System) — Patient + Drug input schema

patient._comment: All patient demographic and clinical fields

labs._comment: Latest lab values — null if not available

box_warning.cv_thrombotic_events: NSAIDs including Diclofenac increase risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events including MI and Stroke. Risk increases with duration of use.
box_warning.gi_bleeding: NSAIDs cause increased risk of serious GI adverse events including bleeding, ulceration and perforation of stomach or intestines, which can be fatal.
box_warning.cabg_contraindicated: Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in the setting of Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) surgery.

contraindications.hypersensitivity_to_drug: Contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to Diclofenac or its excipients.
contraindications.nsaid_allergy: Contraindicated if history of Asthma, Urticaria or allergic-type reactions after Aspirin or other NSAIDs.
contraindications.severe_heart_failure: Contraindicated in severe uncontrolled heart failure.
contraindications.cabg_surgery: Contraindicated in the setting of CABG surgery.
contraindications.pregnancy_third_trimester: Contraindicated from 30 weeks gestation — risk of premature closure of ductus arteriosus.
contraindications.breastfeeding: Contraindicated in breastfeeding women due to potential serious adverse reactions in lactating infants.
contraindications.active_gi_ulcer: Contraindicated in active Gastric/Duodenal/Peptic ulcer, GI bleeding or perforation.
contraindications.severe_hepatic_impairment: Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment or active liver disease.
contraindications.severe_renal_impairment: Contraindicated if CrCl < 30 mL/min or deteriorating renal disease.
contraindications.cerebrovascular_bleeding: Contraindicated in cerebrovascular bleeding or other bleeding disorders.

cv_risk.message: Diclofenac significantly increases cardiovascular thrombotic risk. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration. Consider alternative analgesic. Monitor BP regularly.

gi_risk.message: Increased risk of GI bleeding and ulceration. Co-prescribe PPI (e.g. Omeprazole 20mg OD). Monitor for GI symptoms.

renal_risk.message: Diclofenac can cause renal toxicity and is NOT recommended with moderate-severe renal impairment. Monitor renal function. Use with caution if eGFR 30-60.

hepatic_risk.message: Diclofenac is extensively metabolised hepatically. Not recommended in moderate-severe hepatic impairment. Monitor LFTs periodically.

first.message: Use only if clearly needed. Risk of miscarriage and cardiac malformations reported.

second.message: Use only if clearly needed. Risk of fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios.

third.message: CONTRAINDICATED from 30 weeks gestation — risk of premature closure of ductus arteriosus and prolonged parturition.

breastfeeding.message: Diclofenac is CONTRAINDICATED in breastfeeding. Excreted in breast milk. Risk of serious adverse reactions in the infant.

geriatric.message: Elderly patients have greater risk of NSAID-associated serious CV, GI and renal adverse events. Start at lowest dose. Monitor closely. Use with extreme caution.

pediatric.message: Oral Diclofenac is not recommended in children under 14 years for most indications. Use suppositories for post-operative pain in children under guidance.

alcohol.message: Alcohol combined with NSAIDs significantly increases risk of GI bleeding and hepatotoxicity.

smoking.message: Smoking is an additional risk factor for GI ulceration with NSAID use.

dose_check.message: Recommended Diclofenac oral dose is 50mg TDS (150mg/day). Doses above 200mg/day are not recommended.

allergy.message: Patient has documented allergy to NSAIDs/Diclofenac. USE IS CONTRAINDICATED.

system_wise.Cardiovascular: Congestive heart failure, Hypertension, Tachycardia, Palpitation
system_wise.GI: Dry mouth, Esophagitis, Gastric/peptic ulcer, GI bleeding, Nausea, Vomiting
system_wise.Renal: Acute renal failure, Renal papillary necrosis, Nephrotic syndrome
system_wise.Skin: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, Toxic epidermal necrolysis, Rash

during_treatment: Renal function at 1-2 weeks if risk

drugs.name: Amoxicillin
drugs.document_version: Comprehensive Pin-to-Pin JSON — All Redline Headings & Conditions

mechanism_of_action.step_1: Amoxicillin binds to Penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) on the inner membrane of the bacterial cell wall.
mechanism_of_action.step_2: Inactivation of PBPs interferes with cross-linkage of peptidoglycan chains.
mechanism_of_action.result: Weakening of cell wall and cell lysis.

organisms: Streptococcus species (α- and β-hemolytic, β-lactamase–negative only)
Streptococcus spp. (α- and β-hemolytic, β-lactamase–negative only)

organisms: Streptococcus spp. (α- and β-hemolytic, β-lactamase–negative only)

tonsillitis_and_pharyngitis.population: Adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older

pre_dental_surgery.use_case: Before dental, oral or upper respiratory tract surgery/instrumentation

Mitral valve prolapse with valvular regurgitation

upper_respiratory_skin_genitourinary.children_under_20kg: 20 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses every 6–8 hours

GFR_10_to_30_mL_min.IV: 1 g initially, then 0.5–1 g every 12–24 hours

GFR_less_than_10_mL_min.IV_general: 1 g initially, then 0.5–1 g every 24 hours

drug_administration_instructions: Take orally at the start of a meal.
For IV infusion, dilute to 3% w/v concentration using: Normal Saline (0.9%), Ringer's solution, M/6 Sodium lactate, Hartmann's solution, Glucose 5%, or Sodium chloride 0.18% + Glucose 4%.
Treat Streptococcus pyogenes infections for at least 10 days to prevent acute rheumatic fever.
Continue treatment for minimum 48–72 hours beyond the time the patient becomes asymptomatic or bacterial eradication is confirmed.

contraindications_raw.reason: High risk of erythematous skin rash
Antibiotics have no place in trivial infections

WARNING_1_ANAPHYLACTIC_REACTIONS.title: Anaphylactic / Hypersensitivity Reactions
conditions: Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) reactions reported in patients on Penicillin/Amoxicillin therapy.
Anaphylaxis is more frequent with parenteral therapy but also occurs with oral Penicillins.
Patients with history of Penicillin hypersensitivity may experience severe reactions with Cephalosporins.
Allergic diathesis, Bronchial Asthma, and Hay Fever — special caution required.

Drug-induced Enterocolitis Syndrome (DIES) reported mainly in children: protracted vomiting 1–4 hours after administration, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, hypotension, leukocytosis with neutrophilia; severe cases can progress to shock.
action_required: Careful inquiry about previous hypersensitivity to Penicillins, Cephalosporins, or other allergens before initiating therapy.
DISCONTINUE Amoxicillin immediately if allergic reaction occurs.
Serious anaphylactic reactions require: Epinephrine (immediate), IV steroids, Oxygen, Airway management including intubation.

WARNING_2_SEVERE_CUTANEOUS_ADVERSE_REACT.title: Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reactions (SCAR)
conditions_included: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS)
action_required: Monitor patients closely if skin rash develops.

WARNING_3_SKIN_RASH_MONONUCLEOSIS.title: Skin Rash in Patients with Mononucleosis
WARNING_3_SKIN_RASH_MONONUCLEOSIS.condition: High percentage of patients with mononucleosis develop erythematous skin rash if given Amoxicillin.
WARNING_3_SKIN_RASH_MONONUCLEOSIS.action_required: DO NOT administer Amoxicillin to patients with mononucleosis.

WARNING_4_CDAD.title: Clostridioides Difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD)
conditions: CDAD reported with use of nearly all antibacterial agents including Amoxicillin.
Severity range: mild diarrhoea → fatal colitis.
WARNING_4_CDAD.action_required: Consider CDAD diagnosis in patients with diarrhoea during or after antibiotic use.

WARNING_5_PHENYLKETONURICS.title: Phenylketonurics
conditions: Some Amoxicillin formulations contain Aspartame, which contains Phenylalanine — AVOID in Phenylketonurics.
Oral suspension formulations do NOT contain Phenylalanine — SAFE for Phenylketonurics.

WARNING_6_CARDIOVASCULAR_KOUNIS_SYNDROME.title: Cardiovascular — Kounis Syndrome
WARNING_6_CARDIOVASCULAR_KOUNIS_SYNDROME.condition: Kounis Syndrome (serious allergic reaction that can result in Myocardial Infarction) can occur as chest pain in association with an allergic reaction to Amoxicillin.
WARNING_6_CARDIOVASCULAR_KOUNIS_SYNDROME.action_required: Recognize chest pain in the context of an allergic reaction as potentially Kounis Syndrome.

WARNING_7_HEMATOLOGIC.title: Hematologic — Prolonged Prothrombin Time / Increased INR
conditions: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased INR) reported in patients on Amoxicillin AND oral anticoagulants.
action_required: Adjust oral anticoagulant dose as necessary to maintain desired anticoagulation level.

WARNING_8_RENAL.title: Renal Impairment
conditions: Amoxicillin is primarily excreted by the kidney.
Patients with renal impairment require dose reduction proportional to the degree of renal function loss.
action_required: Periodic assessment of renal function during prolonged therapy.
Cross-reference: Dosage and Administration — Renal Impairment.

WARNING_9_PROLONGED_THERAPY.title: Prolonged Therapy Monitoring
conditions: Elevated liver enzymes and blood count changes reported during prolonged use.
WARNING_9_PROLONGED_THERAPY.action_required: Periodic assessment of renal, hepatic, and hematopoietic functions during prolonged therapy.

WARNING_10_SUPERINFECTIONS.title: Superinfections
conditions: Superinfections with mycotic or bacterial pathogens can occur (commonly Aerobacter, Pseudomonas, Candida).
WARNING_10_SUPERINFECTIONS.action_required: DISCONTINUE Amoxicillin and institute appropriate therapy if superinfection occurs.

WARNING_11_LYMPHATIC_LEUKAEMIA.title: Lymphatic Leukaemia
WARNING_11_LYMPHATIC_LEUKAEMIA.condition: Patients with Lymphatic Leukaemia are susceptible to Amoxicillin-induced skin rashes.
WARNING_11_LYMPHATIC_LEUKAEMIA.action_required: Give Amoxicillin with caution in these patients.

WARNING_12_NON_SUSCEPTIBLE_MICROORGANISM.title: Non-Susceptible Microorganisms
conditions: Not suitable for infections unless pathogen is documented susceptible or highly likely to be susceptible.
Particularly important for: Urinary tract infections, Severe ENT infections.
Amoxicillin is NOT the treatment of choice for sore throat/pharyngitis due to possible underlying infectious mononucleosis.

WARNING_13_CONVULSIONS.title: Convulsions
conditions: Convulsions may occur in patients with impaired renal function.
Convulsions may occur at high doses.
Predisposing factors: history of seizures, treated epilepsy, meningeal disorders.

WARNING_14_JARISCH_HERXHEIMER_REACTION.title: Jarisch-Herxheimer Reaction
WARNING_14_JARISCH_HERXHEIMER_REACTION.condition: Seen following Amoxicillin treatment of Lyme disease — results from bactericidal activity on Borrelia burgdorferi spirochaete.
WARNING_14_JARISCH_HERXHEIMER_REACTION.action_required: Reassure patients that this is common and usually self-limiting.

WARNING_15_CRYSTALLURIA.title: Crystalluria
conditions: Observed very rarely in patients with reduced urine output, predominantly with parenteral therapy.
High urinary Amoxicillin concentrations can cause precipitation in urinary catheters.
action_required: At high doses: maintain adequate fluid intake and urinary output.

WARNING_16_PAEDIATRIC_USE.title: Paediatric Use — Neonates and Premature Children
conditions: Precaution required in premature children and during neonatal period.
Elimination of Amoxicillin may be delayed due to incompletely developed renal function in neonates/young infants.
action_required: Monitor renal, hepatic, and haematological functions.
Modify dosing in pediatric patients 12 weeks or younger.

WARNING_17_EFFECTS_ON_LABORATORY_TESTS.title: Effects on Laboratory Tests
conditions: Amoxicillin may decrease urinary estriol in pregnant women.
High urine concentrations of Ampicillin may cause false-positive reactions for urinary glucose (colorimetric methods).
Amoxicillin may interfere with protein testing (colorimetric methods).
Transient decrease in plasma concentration of: total conjugated estriol, estriol-glucuronide, conjugated estrone, Estradiol — following administration in pregnant women.

drug_drug_interactions.interaction: Decreases renal tubular secretion of Amoxicillin → increased and prolonged blood levels of Amoxicillin
Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased INR)
drug_drug_interactions.clinical_comment: Dose adjustment of oral anticoagulants may be necessary

drug_drug_interactions.interaction: Concurrent use increases incidence of rashes
Amoxicillin may affect intestinal flora → lower estrogen reabsorption → reduced efficacy of combined oral estrogen/progesterone contraceptives
May interfere with the bactericidal effects of Penicillin
Penicillins compete with renal tubular secretion of Methotrexate → decreased clearance → increased Methotrexate serum concentrations and increased toxicity risk

drug_drug_interactions.clinical_comment: Dose adjustment of Digoxin may be necessary

drug_drug_interactions.interaction: Leads to reduction in blood concentrations of Amoxicillin by increased elimination
Amoxicillin may decrease the amount of urinary Estriol in pregnant women

oral.note: No adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed.

parenteral.note: Amoxicillin diffuses across the placenta into fetal circulation. Use when potential benefits outweigh potential risks.

lactation.note: Penicillins are excreted in human milk. May lead to sensitization of infants.
action: Exercise caution when administered to lactating women.
STOP breastfeeding if gastrointestinal disorders (diarrhoea, candidosis, or skin rash) occur in the newborn.

NOT_established: Tonsillitis/Pharyngitis in children younger than 12 years

geriatrics.note: No identified differences in response between elderly (≥65 years) and younger patients, but greater sensitivity cannot be ruled out.
geriatrics.renal_risk: Drug substantially excreted by kidney; risk of toxic reactions greater with impaired renal function.
geriatrics.action: Monitor renal function; care in dose selection.

renal_impairment.note: Primarily eliminated by kidney; dose adjustment required for GFR < 30 mL/min.
renal_impairment.cross_reference: See Dosage and Administration — Renal Impairment
